methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses a multi-center cohort of 120 pancreatic cancer cases and 93 healthy controls and explicitly applies a previously trained miRNA / miRNA+CA19-9 model only on a validation cohort, avoiding circular re-training. However, the control arm excludes clinically relevant comparators (chronic pancreatitis, IPMN) and the authors themselves note that the PC and HC groups differ significantly in age, smoking and diabetes prevalence (p < 0.05), producing uncontrolled confounding. Statistically, AUCs with 95% CIs are reported using pROC and roc.test, but no explicit DeLong p-values, multiplicity correction across the many pairwise/subgroup comparisons, or sample size/power justification are provided, and stage-specific subgroups (e.g., Stage 0 n=6, IB n=6) are very small.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a retrospective case-control diagnostic accuracy study comparing serum biomarkers for pancreatic cancer detection, mapping to Oxford LoE 3b. The clinical question—early detection of a lethal cancer where stage 0-IB disease has >60% 5-year survival versus <3% at stage III-IV—is highly relevant, and the head-to-head comparison showing miRNA+CA19-9 AUC 0.99 versus APOA2 AUC 0.89, including in APOA2-negative patients, directly informs biomarker development. Relevance stops short of practice-changing because the validation is in a case vs. healthy-control design without benign pancreatic disease controls, so real-world screening performance remains unestablished.

reporting_quality.justification: As a diagnostic accuracy study STARD is the applicable standard; the manuscript reports participants, index tests (APOA2-iTQ, CA19-9 Elecsys, QIAseq miRNA NGS on NextSeq 550, DataRobot AutoML v8.0.12), reference standard (histology/cytology ± imaging), and AUCs with 95% CIs, but omits flow diagrams, indeterminate-result handling, blinding of index test interpretation, and adverse events. REMARK-style reporting of the biomarker model (locked thresholds, cut-off derivation, handling of missing data) is limited, and the manuscript does not cite STARD or REMARK. No data or code availability statement is included; miRNA data and DataRobot models are referenced to the prior Kawai et al. paper rather than deposited, and the 100 miRNAs are relegated to Table S1 without repository accession.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty lies in a direct head-to-head comparison of an existing 100-miRNA+CA19-9 model with the APOA2-ATQ/AT isoform biomarker, plus the observation of strong negative correlation (r ≈ -0.62 to -0.63) and complementary behavior in APOA2-negative patients (miRNA+CA19-9 positive in 87% of APOA2-negative cancers). Neither the miRNA panel nor the APOA2 assay is new—both come from published prior work (Kawai et al. 2024; Kashiro et al. 2024)—so the contribution is a focused comparative validation rather than a new biomarker or mechanism. This is a meaningful incremental extension but not field-defining.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is organized in a conventional IMRaD structure with clear tables, ROC figures, and stage-stratified analyses that convey the main quantitative claims. However, the text contains several presentation issues: duplicated abstract paragraphs, inconsistent biomarker nomenclature (APOA2 vs. ApoA2 vs. APOapoA2), two discussion points both numbered 'Eighth', a sign inconsistency where negative correlations are described with positive r values (r = 0.62 / 0.63 in text versus r = -0.62 / -0.63 in the abstract), and an internally inconsistent false-negative count for Stage 0 ('5/6 … 6/6'). These errors are moderate but impede polished communication.

key_strengths: Multi-center serum collection from 14 hospitals with a locked, previously trained miRNA+CA19-9 model evaluated only on a validation cohort, reducing overfitting risk
Clinically meaningful head-to-head comparison showing miRNA+CA19-9 AUC 0.99 (95% CI 0.98-1.00) versus APOA2 AUC 0.89 (95% CI 0.84-0.93), with superiority preserved in stages 0-I and 0-II
Demonstrates complementarity: 87% (47/54) positivity for miRNA+CA19-9 among APOA2-negative cancer patients, supporting combined screening rationale
Transparent and extensive limitations section covering ethnicity, absence of benign pancreatic disease controls, small early-stage subgroups, age confounding, and cost
key_concerns: Case-control design without chronic pancreatitis or IPMN controls limits real-world diagnostic applicability; healthy controls also differ significantly from cases in age, smoking, and diabetes
STARD/REMARK adherence is partial: no flow diagram, no blinding statement, no pre-specified thresholds or multiplicity correction, and no data or code availability statement
Very small early-stage subgroups (Stage 0 n=6, IA n=18, IB n=6) yield unstable stage-specific sensitivity estimates
Multiple textual inconsistencies (duplicated abstract, sign of correlation coefficients, repeated 'Eighth' limitations, inconsistent APOA2 nomenclature, Stage 0 false-negative arithmetic)
Incremental novelty: relies on two previously published biomarker systems; contribution is comparative validation rather than new biology or a new model
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid comparative validation with a convincing AUC advantage for miRNA+CA19-9, but methodological gaps (no benign-disease controls, age/diabetes confounding), partial STARD/REMARK adherence, absent data-sharing, and incremental novelty place the highest plausible acceptance at Tier 3 (e.g., Cancers-level venues) with minor revisions to fix textual inconsistencies and strengthen reporting.
